title: how a note's freshness gets claimed and checked
summary: A note's freshness is a CLAIM the writer makes, not something derived from the note's content: `verified` in a write spec is what causes a file's live hash to be recorded, and read time only compares that recorded hash against the file now. Nothing re-reads the file to decide if a note is still true, so whoever writes decides what counts as verified — which is why a write that carries no knowledge must not stamp.

steps.role: decides what goes in `verified` — the anchor path is added only when the spec carries knowledge implying a read (summary/facets/body); an explicit `verified` from the agent always wins
the only place a hash is produced: for each `verified` path it hashes the file NOW and writes it into the record's anchor. The agent never writes hashes itself
read time — stampAnchors compares each stored anchor hash against the live file and labels the result; since 2026-07-30 that label does not affect rank

invariants: a record with no `verified` carries no hash, and the fold preserves the note's previous hash — so a metadata-only edit cannot reset freshness
freshness has no git dependency: the comparison is hash-vs-file, and `head` is provenance only
